alt: The smallest comma tokenizer: it walks the line once, growing the list buf on every non-comma character and moving it into out whole on every comma, then joining each collected token into text only when it is printed.

steps.c: Python starts at the top of the file. Line 1 runs first.
Line 1 runs; line 4 is next.
Line 4 runs: the name `main` now refers to a function.
Line 21 checks the condition: it is true, so line 22 runs next.
Line 22 calls `main`. A new frame for `main` goes on top of the call stack.
`main()` starts running its body at line 5.
Line 5 runs: `raw` is created with the value `'a,b,c\n'`.
Line 6 runs: `line` is created with the value `'a,b,c'`.
Line 7 runs: `out` is created with the value `[]`. `out` starts empty; it only ever holds finished tokens, each still a list of characters.
Line 8 runs: `buf` is created with the value `[]`. `buf`, the token being built, starts as an empty list of characters.
Line 9 runs: the loop gives `ch` its first value, `'a'`.
Line 10 checks the condition: it is false, so line 14 runs next. A comma means the token building so far is complete.
Line 14 runs: the list that `buf` refers to changes; it is now `['a']`. Any other character is appended to `buf`, never rebuilding it.
Line 9 runs: the loop gives `ch` its next value, `','`.
Line 10 checks the condition: it is true, so line 11 runs next.
Line 11 runs: the list that `out` refers to changes; it is now `[['a']]`. `buf` itself moves into `out`, unjoined; no characters are copied here.
Line 12 runs: `buf` changes from `['a']` to `[]`. `buf` resets to an empty list, ready for the next token.
Line 9 runs: the loop gives `ch` its next value, `'b'`.
Line 10 checks the condition: it is false, so line 14 runs next.
Line 14 runs: the list that `buf` refers to changes; it is now `['b']`.
Line 9 runs: the loop gives `ch` its next value, `','`.
Line 10 checks the condition: it is true, so line 11 runs next.
Line 11 runs: the list that `out` refers to changes; it is now `[['a'], ['b']]`.
Line 12 runs: `buf` changes from `['b']` to `[]`.
Line 9 runs: the loop gives `ch` its next value, `'c'`.
Line 10 checks the condition: it is false, so line 14 runs next.
Line 14 runs: the list that `buf` refers to changes; it is now `['c']`.
Line 9: the loop has no values left, so it ends and line 15 runs next.
Line 15 checks the condition: it is true, so line 16 runs next. This check only fires when something is left unfinished after the loop.
Line 16 runs: the list that `out` refers to changes; it is now `[['a'], ['b'], ['c']]`. In the trailing-comma preset, `buf` is already empty here, so nothing is added.
Line 17 runs: the loop gives `t` its first value, `['a']`.
Line 18 runs: it prints `a`. Each token is joined into text only now, once, right before it is printed.
Line 17 runs: the loop gives `t` its next value, `['b']`.
Line 18 runs: it prints `b`.
Line 17 runs: the loop gives `t` its next value, `['c']`.
Line 18 runs: it prints `c`.
The call of `main` returns `None`. Its frame leaves the call stack next.
The program has finished: no lines are left to run.
